name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,442

clue.text: Factory fund for housing for young climbers?

blocks.note: a plant is a factory or works
a pot is a pool or fund of money

explanation.surface: A factory's fund to provide homes for young mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The young climbers are seedlings of climbing plants such as ivy, not junior mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A container of soil holds growing seedlings, including those of ivy or clematis that will later scramble upward.

clue.text: Cloth cap on posh boy has head of idiot inside

indicators.note: a cap is the top, so only the opening letter of that word is used
the head of a word is its first letter
inside means placed within the other piece

blocks.note: first letter
a lad is a boy
first letter

explanation.surface: A posh boy wears a cloth cap with an idiot's head beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a tartan woollen fabric, a type of patterned textile.

clue.text: Indy setter upset Celtic hooligan set straight in a row?

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Gila is a setter of the Independent's crosswords
ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: An Independent setter is upset that a Celtic hooligan was put straight during a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Glasgow football club; ned is Scottish for a lout. 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Things arranged in a straight line, matching up with one another, are said to be lined up this way.

clue.text: Bank clerk bringing in vans to recover any VW Polo?

indicators.note: bringing something in means taking it inside, so this piece holds the other
vans are vanguards or fronts, so only the leading letter of each word is used

blocks.note: a teller works at a bank counter
first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A bank clerk brings in recovery vans to retrieve somebody's stolen Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'VW Polo' reads as the hatchback, but VW is only fodder: Polo is Marco Polo, the Venetian who journeyed to China. A van is the front, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo journeyed overland from Venice to the court of Kublai Khan, so he was the archetypal explorer and wayfarer.

clue.text: Worked hard, having no time to get lubricated

indicators.note: having none of something means that letter is removed

blocks.note: to toil is to work hard
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone worked hard with no time off and turned to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Lubricated can also mean drunk, which the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine part given grease or oil to run smoothly has been treated with lubricant.

clue.text: Break America after success touring Austria

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a hit is a success
A is the international vehicle code for Austria
the United States

explanation.surface: A band takes a break from America after a hit record and a tour of Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the international vehicle code for Austria, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or gap in continuity, an interruption in activity, is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: One Direction to institute legal proceedings against kids

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
S is south, a compass direction
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: The band One Direction suing children.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a boy band, split here into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal legal term for a person's children or offspring.

clue.text: Very concerning to come across a betrayal

indicators.note: coming across something means stretching over it, so the outer piece goes around it

blocks.note: tres is French for very
on means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Coming across a betrayal is very worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: TRESON goes round A after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign, the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Adore cast being entertained by Sid's little ways?

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are scattered and reset
a guest entertained is held inside, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor adores a cast entertained by Sid's quirky habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ways' looks like habits; here it means roads, and little ones are minor routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor lanes that branch off a main route are small thoroughfares, hence little ways.

clue.text: Tape bag up, then most of Hoskins?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned around
most of a word means all but its final letter

blocks.note: a sac is a bag or pouch
Hoskins is this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: Bag up the tape, then that's most of Hoskins done.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is the compiler of this crossword, so his name stands for SETTER, which then loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio cassette is a plastic case holding a reel of magnetic recording tape.

clue.text: An epic fail going topless with this woman

indicators.note: losing the top means the first letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: the indefinite article
epic means huge in scale
taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman going topless turns out to be an epic fail.
explanation.walkthrough: A + BIG + (F)AIL gives ABIGAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a female given name, so this woman can be called by it.

clue.text: Quickly polish off 70% of sweetmeats, then go Dutch

indicators.note: eating up seven tenths of a ten-letter word leaves only its final three letters

blocks.note: the last three of its ten letters survive
to go is a euphemism for urinating
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: Eat most of the sweets quickly, then split the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go Dutch' looks like sharing a bill; it is split into a toilet euphemism and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving rapidly, with great velocity, is the idiomatic sense of this two-word phrase used as an adverb.

clue.text: Old linesman is finished, so the radio said

indicators.note: what is heard over the radio is spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: finished means completed, a word sounding like the poet's surname

explanation.surface: A radio report says an old football linesman has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: John Donne, the 17th-century poet, wrote lines of verse; the surface suggests a football assistant referee.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a seventeenth-century metaphysical poet, a writer of verse lines, hence a whimsical linesman from long ago.

clue.text: Depression not over, off to see pharmacist?

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to drop the letter standing for a cricket over
off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Depression lingering, someone heads off to see the pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O out of DEPRESSION and rearrange the rest. The question mark admits the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist makes up and hands out medicines, so is one who dispenses drugs.

clue.text: Training a bad lot to change is a craft

indicators.note: the letters are told to alter, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school training
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Reforming a bad lot of young offenders is a skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like skill, as in training as a trade; here it means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small vessel propelled by pushing foot pedals is a boat, and any boat is a watercraft.

clue.text: Dying fire fed by the last two bits of kindling

indicators.note: something fed takes in food, so this piece takes the other inside it
only the final pair of letters of the word is used

blocks.note: fire means passion or ardour
its final two letters

explanation.surface: A dying fire is fed with the last bits of kindling.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a gentle euphemism for to die, so the present participle means departing this life.

clue.text: Honestly, Dicky, in a way that's quite sneaky

definitions.text: in a way that's quite sneaky

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Honestly, Dicky, you behave rather sneakily.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name being addressed; it is slang for wonky.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly, covertly or furtively, so others do not notice, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Conservative lass missing the last line dance

indicators.note: missing the last means the final letter is lost

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative
a gal is a girl

explanation.surface: A Conservative girl sits out the final line dance of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed by people in a single snaking file, each holding the one in front.

clue.text: Had a go at new crash diets, but not runs

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are arranged into a new order
but not tells us to leave out the letter that follows

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone tried new crash diets but gave up running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a go at' suggests attempting; here it is the idiom for scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at someone is British idiom for criticising or rebuking them severely.

clue.text: Very liberal artist with backing of The Sun

indicators.note: backing means going in the reverse direction, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: so means very
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A very liberal artist has the support of The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper in the surface; here it is the star.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or derived from the sun, as in solar power.

clue.text: Permit nits to go on top of Norman church

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

blocks.note: nits are lice and their eggs
first letter
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Permission for nits to go on top of a Norman church.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman suggests the architecture, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is an official document or permission authorising someone to do something.

clue.text: Tense Afghan province left by large American division?

indicators.note: left by means abandoned by, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
Helmand is a province of southern Afghanistan
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
US means American

explanation.surface: A tense Afghan province abandoned by a large American army division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' sounds military, but it is a social split between two camps. Helmand was where British troops fought in Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an us-versus-them split between two opposed camps, a social divide.

clue.text: Let down recently (after making love Ed turned over)

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the name is read backwards
making one thing into another means a letter is swapped for a new piece

blocks.note: taken as written
of late means recently
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Ed rolled over after lovemaking and felt let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making love' looks like sex, but it instructs: turn the O of OF LATE into backwards Ed.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to release its air, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Where people might catch a live bass together?

definitions.text: Where people might catch a live bass

blocks.clueFragment: Where people might catch a live bass
blocks.note: first meaning: at a live music performance, where a bass guitarist plays
second meaning: acting jointly

explanation.surface: Anglers working together hope to land a live bass.
explanation.walkthrough: The bass reads as a fish to be caught; it is the bass player heard live on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at a live gig, and also means jointly or in cooperation with others.

clue.text: Tend to hold on to a pint, but not neck it

definitions.text: hold on to a pint, but not neck it

blocks.note: first meaning: look after someone who is ill

blocks.clueFragment: hold on to a pint, but not neck it
blocks.note: second meaning: drink slowly, making a pint last

explanation.surface: A drinker tends to sip a pint slowly rather than gulping it.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck a drink is British slang for gulping it down.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to care for a patient, and also to cradle a drink, sipping it slowly to make it last.

clue.text: Sailor on island with son breaking bones

indicators.note: breaking in means splitting the other piece and sitting in the gap

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
I is the abbreviation for island
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A sailor stranded on an island with his son breaks some bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small ankle bones of the foot, so the plural names a set of bones.

clue.text: Nobs and heartless tycoons? Rotten to the core!

indicators.note: with the heart cut out only the ends of the word are kept
placed at the core means set in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: first and last letters only
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: Posh people and ruthless business tycoons are rotten through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: Toffs is British slang for upper-class people, as is nobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for wealthy, upper-class people of high social standing.

clue.text: Places one might find rakes in Slough society

blocks.note: to slough is to cast off, like a snake's skin
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Where you might find rakes, dissolute men, in Slough's society.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town near London; it is the verb. Rakes are garden tools, not cads.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden outbuildings store tools such as rakes and spades, so they are where you would find them.

clue.text: Dope time with Latin woman in uniform?

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information, as is dope
an era is a period of time
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: Spending time with a Latin woman in uniform, perhaps for drug information.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a senior army officer, here a woman, wears uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking army officer wears military dress, and that officer could be a woman.

clue.text: Some fresh aperitifs in fashion again?

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are used

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Refreshing aperitifs are back in fashion again.
explanation.definitionFit: To form or mould something into a different shape a second time; fashion is used as a verb meaning form.

clue.text: Wanted: new editors to cover Spain

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
two editors, each ED
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A job advert: new editors wanted to cover Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural editors gives ED twice, and E sits inside after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Required or lacked is the sense here, as in an item someone had a need for.

clue.text: Free of flatulence? Not so much after turn

blocks.note: to wind is to turn, as a key or a handle
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone's digestive troubles ease after a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the second piece after the first. The question mark flags the jokey definition: a still day has no wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any breeze, a calm day is without air movement; the clue treats gas as the other sense.
